🇲🇽📺 <u>Mexico restores audience rights: separate news from opinion, ads from content</u>

The telecom regulator (CRT) approved new audience-rights guidelines requiring open TV and radio to give the public truthful information, clearly separate news from opinion and advertising from content, guarantee the right of reply, and protect minors — protections gutted in the neoliberal era under media-industry pressure. Refined from 8,889 public comments and effective 30 days after publication, the rules stop short of policing content: the regulator says it won't judge which news is true or false, only that outlets honor the complaint process. (El Soberano)

🇲🇽🕵️ <u>Declassified: the old regime spied on Julio Scherer for 20+ years</u>

Files show Mexico's Cold War political police, the DFS, surveilled crusading journalist Julio Scherer for more than two decades — from 1959 until the government-engineered coup of July 8, 1976 that pushed him out of Excélsior. The pre-4T security state kept a file on the free press it could neither buy nor silence.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRI boss "Alito" loses two ex-aides to corruption arrests</u>

Campeche's anti-corruption prosecutors arrested two former officials tied to PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno within 48 hours — his brother's accountant and his ex-communications chief — over a scheme that diverted 36 million pesos through shell companies issuing simulated invoices. Prosecutors say the new evidence can weigh on the pending process to strip Moreno's immunity.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Ayotzinapa: 10 new suspects identified — and detained</u>

President Sheinbaum told the families of the 43 that new cell-phone and forensic analysis identified "10 people who had not been linked to the case" and made calls tied to the forced disappearance — all now in custody. She asked that the findings be published before the September 26 anniversary and pledged to press pending extraditions from abroad. Twelve years on, the 4T keeps pulling the thread earlier governments cut.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Morena hands the Senate gavel to a veteran — and stands up a Women's Secretariat</u>

Veteran senator Higinio Martínez takes the Senate presidency on September 1 by consensus of Morena's caucus, as Laura Itzel Castillo leaves the post to head the newly created federal Secretaría de las Mujeres under President Sheinbaum. A governing bloc reshuffling its own leadership and standing up a new ministry for women in the same move.

🇲🇽💵 <u>The superpeso shrugs off the Fed</u>

Fed chair Kevin Warsh used his Jackson Hole speech to signal more rate hikes, pushing the dollar back above 17 pesos (17.03). Even so, El Financiero notes the peso is still up 5.29% this year — from 18.01 to 17.05 per dollar — outrunning its emerging-market peers. One hawkish speech doesn’t erase a year of the superpeso.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PAN keeps collapsing — now it’s lost Coahuila</u>

Mexico’s right-wing PAN just lost its official registration in Coahuila after scraping barely 2.1% in June’s local elections, erasing its seats in the state congress. Once the party of Fox and Calderón, it can no longer clear the threshold to legally exist in a northern state it used to contest.
